title: Hand agents transition recipes, not vibes
principle: Jakub Antalik’s transitions.dev: essential UI transitions as copy-paste recipes (CSS/React) and coding-agent skills beat ‘make it smooth’ prompts. Give the agent a named free recipe, ink-adapted tokens, and reduced-motion rules so motion stays craft—not improvised slop.
procedure: Pick a free transitions.dev recipe that matches the job (reveal, tab underline, success check, skeleton, etc.).
Paste or attach the recipe as an agent skill/reference; forbid inventing novel easing stacks when a recipe fits.
Adapt colors/easing to your design tokens (Quiet Folio: ink/paper, short durations).
Require prefers-reduced-motion handling from the recipe or your override.
Critic: motion should match purposeful-motion + animation-restraint—delete if frequency is too high.
Smoke-test interruptibility: trigger twice quickly—motion should retarget, not restart awkwardly.
examplePrompts:
Implement motion using transitions.dev free recipes (Jakub Antalik)—not freeform animation:
1) Choose recipe: texts-reveal OR number-pop-in OR skeleton-reveal OR success-check (free tier only).
2) Adapt to tokens: paper #FAF9F7, ink #221C24, duration ≤240ms, ease-out.
3) Wire prefers-reduced-motion.
4) Do not use Pro recipes; do not add purple glow.
Return which recipe + diff.
Replace this custom keyframed bounce with the closest free transitions.dev pattern. If none fit, delete the animation per animation-restraint.
promptWhy: Named recipe constraint stops model-invented bounce soup.
Token adaptation keeps Quiet Folio identity while reusing proven motion.
tips: This site’s motion lab already adapts free recipes—see /motion and sources.
Agent-ready skills on transitions.dev are designed for coding agents.
Pair with Emil’s purpose/frequency checks before installing a recipe.
Prefer CSS transitions for interruptible UI chrome; pair with purposeful-motion.

antiPatterns: ‘Make it silky’ with no recipe reference.
Mixing five easings on one page.
checklist: Frequency check passed or motion deleted.
Recipe name recorded in PR/commit message.
